tonight.headline: Sadiq is questionable after three limited practices; the flex is still a point off
body: The bad news didn't resolve: Kenyon Sadiq, your only tight end, was limited again on Friday and is officially questionable with his back, and the Ravens D/ST lost Trey Hendrickson to a finger procedure. ESPN has you at 123.1 against Team 13's 88.3, 68%, because their lineup still carries two players who are ruled out.

Two things before Sunday. The flex still has Tuten where the projection prefers Downs by a point: a coin flip, so take the projection, before 07:30 (card 1). And at 09:30 Sunday check the Jets' inactives: if Sadiq is out, Mark Andrews is still a free agent and has no game status.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Team 13 still start DeVonta Smith and Rachaad White, both ruled out on Friday (PhiladelphiaEagles.com; NFL.com status list 2 Oct), at 0.0 each. On their bench: DJ Moore 13.0, Dalton Kincaid 10.7, Blake Corum 8.1 and Lamar Jackson, who came off Baltimore's report. Josh Allen has no designation.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Team 13 moving Moore and Corum in for Smith and White: about 21 projected points back, which takes 88.3 to roughly 109 and the gap to about 14.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sun 07:30 Mexico City (Downs locks in London)
doFirst.title: Put Downs back in the flex over Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: 13.7 to 12.7. Carried for a fourth run and still not done. A coin flip, so it goes to the projection — and no thesis.

case.label: The rule
case.body: lineup_check.py: 'start Josh Downs 13.7 over Bhayshul Tuten 12.7 — COIN FLIP, take the projection.' Neither has a game status: Indianapolis ruled nobody out and Downs was never listed (Colts.com; NFL.com 2 Oct); Tuten was off Jacksonville's report all week (Bengals.com 2 Oct).

case.label: The player
case.body: Downs drew 11 targets in Week 3, a third of Indianapolis' (archive), with Pierce on IR. Keenan Allen is now officially questionable (rest/groin) after three limited days (NBC; NFL.com 2 Oct): if he sits, Downs' share grows, and that isn't in the 13.7. Washington have allowed the most points to receivers (footballdb, standard scoring).

case.label: The timing cost
case.body: Downs locks at 07:30 in London, Tuten at 11:00. Putting Downs in the flex gives up a little late flexibility, but nothing on this roster is waiting on a later inactive except Sadiq, and only a tight end covers him.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Tuten outscores Downs. It's a coin flip: this is the expected-value call, not a prediction, and it gets no decision-log entry.

doFirst.sources: lineup_check.py · Colts.com · NFL.com · Bengals.com · NBC · footballdb · Week 3 archive

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · if Sadiq is inactive at Sun 09:30 Mexico City; both lock at 11:00
doFirst.title: If Sadiq sits: add Mark Andrews, drop Carnell Tate
doFirst.subtitle: Carried, and now a Sunday-morning check: Sadiq is questionable, not out. Andrews is still a free agent, so it's an add with no priority cost.

case.label: The injury
case.body: Sadiq hurt his back on a diving touchdown catch in Week 3 and was limited Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; he's questionable (Bleacher Nation; NBC; RotoWire 2 Oct). No coach has spoken to his availability. Mason Taylor (thumb) and Adonai Mitchell (finger) are ruled out, so if he plays the role is large. DraftKings Network says sit him because his game is yards after the catch; that's an opinion about effectiveness, not availability. ESPN: QUESTIONABLE at 9.9.

case.label: The fallback
case.body: Andrews projects 10.1 at home to Tennessee and carries no game status after full practices with a hand listing (NFL.com status list 2 Oct; NBC 30 Sep); he runs a route on 65.6% of dropbacks with 23.7% of the targets (FantasyPros 1 Oct, carried). Zay Flowers is questionable after a limited Friday the Ravens called rest (Ravens.com 2 Oct). He's a FREEAGENT in this snapshot: an add, not a claim, and anyone else can make it first. If he's gone: Hockenson (9.1, 14:05) or Darren Waller (9.3), who plays Sunday night against the defence allowing the most points to tight ends.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Carnell Tate, the fifth receiver and not on the screen's exposure list. Kamara and Gordon are on it, and Golden and Downs both project above him, so none of them is the drop.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: It fires and Andrews scores less than the best free tight end that week (Hunter Henry, Loveland).

whatWentWrong.title: The flex has sat a point below the projection since Wednesday night
whatWentWrong.lead: Downs went into the flex at 14:10 Wednesday and back out for Tuten at 21:31 that night, Mexico City time. Four briefs later it hasn't moved.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: Section 0 of the strategy: every Week 1–2 loss was winnable with the roster owned, and the most expensive mistake was overriding the projection. A one-point flip isn't a disaster; the habit is.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: News ESPN hasn't priced about Downs or Tuten. The one new item cuts toward Downs: Keenan Allen is questionable.

worthALook.name: Bills D/ST
worthALook.lead: The D/ST comparison: the Bills are free at 8.0 and the Ravens fell to 7.0. Still a hold, and here's why.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Bills 8.0 at home to New England, the wire's biggest riser at +5.80; Drake Maye will play, having practised in full with a sore shoulder (Vrabel, Boston 25, 2 Oct). Ravens 7.0 at home to Tennessee after Trey Hendrickson was ruled out following a finger procedure; Minter calls the absence 'very, very short term' (Ravens.com 2 Oct). The Steelers, 8.2 on paper, played Thursday.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: The gap is exactly 1.0: inside the two-point coin-flip line, and the D/ST seat changed hands on Wednesday. This morning's row said a one-point gap with Hendrickson out would change it. That condition has fired, and I'm still holding: it was written against the churn rule, which closes a seat for seven days unless the player in it is ruled out. A defence missing one rusher isn't ruled out.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Ravens' number falling two points below a free defence that hasn't kicked off.

worthALook.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
worthALook.lead: The kicker comparison: 0.1 better than Myers and now a free agent. Hold.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Fairbairn 9.8, Myers 9.7. He's a free agent and costs no priority, but the kicker seat changed hands on Wednesday and a tenth of a point isn't a reason to change it again. Myers isn't on Seattle's final report (Seahawks.com 2 Oct).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers appearing on Seattle's report.

doNotChase.name: Darren Waller
doNotChase.lead: The biggest riser among players, and a tight end: tempting with Sadiq questionable, and still third in line.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 8 targets and 10.1 points in Week 3 (archive), most of it after Jalen Coker left with a quad injury. Coker is questionable after a limited Friday and Canales decides Saturday (Panthers.com 2 Oct); Xavier Legette is out. Waller himself has no game status.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He projects 9.3, below Andrews (10.1) and Sadiq (9.9), and adding him today costs a roster seat for a player who doesn't start unless Sadiq sits. 2 and 3 targets in Weeks 1–2 (archive): the role appeared when Coker left and may leave when he returns.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Sadiq inactive at 09:30 Sunday with Andrews already taken: then Waller is a live fallback, because he plays Sunday night against Detroit, who allow the most points to tight ends (footballdb), and stays addable all afternoon.

doNotChase.name: Kendre Miller
doNotChase.lead: The wire's biggest running-back riser, and the other half of a backfield you already own.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Travis Etienne went on IR, and Kellen Moore said 'Alvin and Kendre will handle that load really well' (CBS 1 Oct). After the injury the carries went Kamara 6, Miller 4 (ESPN's Terrell via Heavy 2 Oct), and the Saints added Ulysses Bentley IV to the practice squad.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 4 carries and 3 targets for 3.9 points in Week 3 (archive), 15 touches all season. You own Kamara, the lead half, who projects 10.6 to Miller's 8.8 and still sits on your bench.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Miller out-touching Kamara on Monday night: then Kamara is the problem to solve, not a reason to own both.

doNotChase.name: Jaylen Wright
doNotChase.lead: Cleared for Sunday after two full practices; he's splitting the backfield you spent priority on.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Limited Wednesday with the foot, full Thursday and Friday, no designation (Vikings.com; NBC 2 Oct). Hafley: 'should be good to go'. Fowler: Miami 'plans to use both' (ESPN via Yahoo).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He'd be a fifth back on a roster that starts two, at Minnesota, who allow the 4th-fewest points to RBs (footballdb) and haven't given up a rushing touchdown (Yahoo 2 Oct). A free agent, but a roster seat is still a cost. ESPN: 7.5 to Gordon's 9.0.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wright takes over Miami outright (Gordon under 8 touches) — then Gordon is the problem to solve, not a reason to own both.
